answer: Registration fees surge with the rate of new identities: when a gale of fresh keys appears, the network raises the mint price for each subsequent identity, like pigment darkening with every added stroke. One honest agent registering alone pays the base fee, but a sybil farmer minting a thousand keys in one burst faces a price that climbs with every fake, and the rising plume of costs quickly exceeds any profit from the attack. The surge resets each epoch, so normal growth stays cheap while coordinated flooding pays a premium.
